events.title: Storytime with Seina Wedlick
events.description: Join us as we welcome local author Seina Wedlick back to the store to celebrate her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller, about a girl who fills the starry, moonlit sky with magical tales. Every night, Noor listens for the sound of the gong and the storyteller's drum. Gong, Gong, Gong! Tap! Tap! Tap! With each beat, fantastic tales swirl and sway and unfold around her. One night, she waits and waits, but no drumbeat comes her way. Can Noor tap the drum and keep the storyteller's magic alive? Find out in this modern fairy tale about a young Nigerian girl who taps stories on her drum and carries tradition in her heart.
events.blurb: Meet local author Seina Wedlick at Linden Tree Books and hear her read from her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller.

events.title: Book Launch with Nathan Hale — In conversation with Nidhi Chanani
events.description: We are incredibly excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Nathan Hale to the store to celebrate the launch of Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales: The Web of War! Nathan will be in conversation with bestselling author Nidhi Chanani. After their conversation, Nathan and Nidhi will battle in an old-fashioned, no-holds-barred draw-off! This event is free, but you must purchase a copy of The Web of War from Linden Tree to enter the signing line. Books can be purchased with an event ticket, in person at Linden Tree, or on our website. In the summer of 1944, the Allied forces carried out the largest seaborne invasion in military history. American, British, and Canadian soldiers took to the skies and the sand, bombarding the beaches of Normandy, France, in the famous operation known as D-Day. This pivotal battle turned the tides against the Nazis, but how did the French find themselves overtaken by enemy forces to begin with? How did Hitler and his Nazi ideology sweep through Germany so quickly? And how did American military service members and civilians, from generals, to war correspondents, to heroic Black soldiers, work together to defeat the Nazi government and bring an end to Hitler's reign of terror? In The Web of War, history is in your hands! Pick your path and unravel the thrilling, shocking, gruesome, and true stories of the Second World War in this all-new hazardous tale.
events.blurb: Meet author-illustrator Nathan Hale at Linden Tree Books and hear him in conversation with author Nidhi Chanani about his new Hazardous Tales book.

events.title: I Am Human: Storytime + Creative Writing Workshop
events.description: Calling All Humans! Join author-illustrator Laura G. Lee for a special I Am Human book launch, storytime, and creative workshop. Laura will begin with a reading of I Am Human and a playful conversation inspired by the book: What does it mean to be human? How are we different from AI—and how do we know? After the reading, participants are invited to join a hands-on writing and drawing workshop, responding to creative prompts through words and pictures, enjoying snacks, and sharing ideas. All ages are welcome. The workshop is especially well suited to older elementary kids, teens, and adults, while younger children are welcome to enjoy the story time portion with their families. Workshop RSVPs are encouraged so we can prepare enough materials.
events.blurb: Hear Laura G. Lee read I Am Human, then join a playful conversation about what it means to be human.

events.title: Book Launch with Lily Berlin Dodd — In conversation with Misa Sugiura
events.description: We're excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author Lily Berlin Dodd back to the store to celebrate the launch of the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series, The First Flame! Lily will be in conversation with author Misa Sugiura. With Eva locked away in Byrdhaven and Rubi missing, all Dusty can do is avoid capture and (attempt to) sleep through his nightmares in the wake of Cal's death. When fate leads Dusty back to the Lockwood Inn, he overhears the next stage of Eoin Parnassus' sinister plans for aerimanders, and knows he must do everything in his power to stop it. Dodging strict nuns, wanted posters, seasickness, altitude sickness, a clockwork army, and a perilously evil clown on the way, Myrnie, Eva, and Dusty are willing to fight to the ends of the Earth--or at least the edges of their map--to stop Eoin Parnassus, Director of Kingdom Secrets. But Rubi is hiding a shocking truth and Parnassus may pose an even bigger threat than they could ever have imagined. Who can be trusted when secrets lurk around every corner of the Kingdom?
events.blurb: Hear Lily Berlin Dodd talk with author Misa Sugiura about The First Flame, the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series.

events.title: Storytime with Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon
events.description: Join us as we welcome Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon to celebrate their empowering new picture book, No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her journey to finding her voice, independence, and freedom on a skateboard. Kanya Sesser was born without legs, but that doesn't mean she has limits! Sometimes I still fall. But I never give up. I make things work for me. Because I'm strong. Because I'm free. Because I have NO limits. Kanya Sesser has spent her life sharing the message that no matter what life deals you, you can do anything. In this picture book based on her childhood, she tells the story of how she first learned to stand up for herself, both on a skateboard and in life. When people grab her wheelchair to push her to class or onto the bus after school, she's too shocked and too sad to say no. The people around her don't understand that she moves herself. But when she rides a skateboard for the first time, she experiences a new sense of freedom and joy, and she finally finds her voice.
events.blurb: Meet authors Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon at Linden Tree Books and hear their picture book No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her skateboarding journey.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! The club is led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee. We hope to introduce interested readers to amazing new books and the opportunity to talk about them in a fun, relaxed group setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle-solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Free, 50-person maximum. Story Time tickets required. Another event, Music and Movement B, will start at 11:15 for those that weren't able to make it inside for this event. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. events.title: Reading Buddies
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a volunteer. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our volunteers will listen to children read and provide support in phonics, sight words, and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the West Valley Branch Library. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating children.
events.attendanceNote: Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating children.

events.title: Athena Project
events.description: Spark curiosity and discover the joy of learning with the Athena Project! This interactive enrichment program for students in grades 2–5 combines the principles of classical education with hands-on activities that bring mathematics, language arts, history, science, and literature to life. Through games, crafts, experiments, storytelling, role-play, and collaborative projects, participants will strengthen critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and communication skills while exploring new ideas in a supportive and engaging environment. Every session is designed to inspire confidence, curiosity, and a lifelong love of learning. Ages: 7-11 (2nd grade to 5th grade). Registration recommended.
events.blurb: Have grades 2-5 dive into hands-on activities blending math, language arts, history, and science at the Athena Project.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K-3 and will be held in the Reading to Children corner, within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring your child to hear a volunteer read aloud in a small group at Berryessa Library.

events.title: Reading to Furry Friends
events.description: Tell a story to a Furry Friend! Children are invited to practice reading to gentle, trained assistance dogs who love books! The main objective of this program is to provide a relaxed and "dog-friendly" atmosphere, which allows students to practice the skill of reading. By sitting down next to a dog and reading to the dog, all threats of being judged are put aside: the child relaxes, pats the attentive dog, and focuses on the reading. This program occurs on the 1st Saturday of each month. This program is presented by Furry Friends Pet Assisted Therapy Services. Please do not bring your own dogs or other pets. Free. No registration required. ¡Cuéntale un cuento a un amigo mascota! Invitamos a los niños a practicar la lectura con perros de asistencia amables y entrenados ¡a los que les encantan los libros! El objetivo principal de este programa es ofrecer un ambiente relajado y acogedor para los perros, permitiendo así que los estudiantes practiquen sus habilidades de lectura. Al sentarse junto a un perro y leerle, desaparece el temor a ser juzgados: el niño se relaja, acaricia al atento animal y se concentra en la lectura. Este programa se lleva a cabo el primer sábado de cada mes. Este programa es presentado por Furry Friends Pet Assisted Therapy Services. Por favor, no traiga sus propios perros ni mascotas. Actividad gratuita. No requiere inscripción.
events.blurb: Read a story aloud to a gentle, trained therapy dog in a relaxed, low-pressure setting.

events.title: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: We are living in a world that feels increasingly unpredictable and unstable, where our daily lives are shifting faster than ever before. Knowing how to tap into our inner resources to navigate stress and uncertainty is crucial. Join our volunteer Snow for a mindfulness program offering practical, evidence-based mindfulness tools that will help you enhance your attention and focus, regulate your emotions and cultivate calm and resilience in your daily life. Snow Bai has a Master's in Psychology and Neuroscience in Mental Health at King's College London and has professional training in Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) from the Oxford Mindfulness Foundation. Free. No registration required. Beginners are welcome.
events.blurb: Sit down for a mindfulness meditation session at Willow Glen Library, focused on handling stress and uncertainty in everyday life.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club: Beginning (Tiếng Việt)
events.description: Xây dựng kỹ năng giao tiếp với những người học trình độ mới bắt đầu khác trong một môi trường chào đón và tôn trọng. Los participantes aprenderán los conceptos básicos del dibujo, comenzando con líneas de boceto y formas, y aplicarán estas habilidades para diseñar divertidas y expresivas obras de arte con emojis. events.title: Evergreen Branch Library's 20th Anniversary Celebration

Live Entertainment and Activities: Cultural dance performance by Jayendra Kalakendra; Cultural dance performance by Ensamble Folclórico Colibrí; Balloon art giveaway; Face painting; Giant bubble play stations; Grab-and-go craft kits*; Prize wheel*; Prize drawing*; Refreshments*. *While supplies last. Share Your Story: Share your Evergreen Branch story and help us celebrate 20 years by telling us about a favorite memory, experience, or special moment. Did you know? Evergreen Branch is home to Discoveries, a public artwork by Larry Kirkland featuring three white marble sculptures of an ear, mouth, and eye that celebrate learning and discovery through our senses. Stop by and check it out during your next visit. Special Thanks: This event has been generously sponsored by the San José Public Library Foundation, Friends of the Evergreen Branch Library, and Friends of the West Valley Branch Library.

events.title: The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist
events.description: Join us at Cupertino Library for a special documentary viewing of The AI Doc: Or How I Became An Apocaloptimist. events.title: Everyone Can Create: Beginning Stop Motion Animation

events.title: STEAM Sunday: Fall Sensory Bottles
events.description: The worlds of science and art collide at STEAM Sundays. We'll provide the supplies; you bring your curious and creative energy! For November, we'll be celebrating the fall season as we create sensory bottles. We'll discuss density, buoyancy, mixtures, and solutions, then we'll explore what we learned as we combine ingredients for our craft. We'll also chat about seasonal changes, how they impact the world around us, and how sensory objects can help us refocus and reset. Participants will leave with their very own ready-to-use sensory bottle. Through a brief lecture and hands-on experimenting and creating, STEAM Sundays allow participants to learn about science, technology, engineering, and math while working on an art project. After learning about a topic, the experimentation and note taking parts of the scientific process will be conducted through a craft. Everyone will go home with a finished project and a better understanding of each chosen topic. Best for youth ages 5-12. Supplies are limited; registration required. Después, pondremos en práctica lo aprendido al combinar diferentes materiales para crear nuestra manualidad. También conversaremos sobre los cambios de estación, cómo afectan al mundo que nos rodea y cómo los objetos sensoriales pueden ayudarnos a recuperar la concentración y encontrar la calma. ¡Cada participante se llevará a casa su propia botella sensorial, lista para usar! A través de una breve lección, experimentos y creaciones prácticas, los domingos STEAM permiten a los participantes aprender sobre ciencia, tecnología, ingeniería y matemáticas mientras trabajan en un proyecto de arte. Después de aprender sobre cierto tema, la experimentación y el tomar apuntes de este proceso científico se llevarán a cabo por medio de una artesanía. Todos irán a casa con un proyecto terminado y con un mejor entendimiento de cada tema elegido. Para niños y niñas de 5 a 12 años. Los materiales son limitados. Se requiere inscripción previa.

events.title: The GreenRoots Collective: Environmental Technology Workshops
events.description: Discover how science and engineering can be used to understand and solve real environmental challenges. In this hands-on Green Roots Collective workshop series, students will explore sustainability through interactive experiments, engineering challenges, collaborative problem-solving, and community-focused projects. Sustainability is becoming an increasingly important part of the world students are growing up in. Understanding how the environment works, and how everyday decisions, technology, and engineering can help protect it, gives young learners the tools to think critically about real-world problems and envision better solutions for the future. Rather than simply learning environmental concepts, students will put them into practice. Each workshop introduces a scientific idea, gives students the opportunity to investigate it through a hands-on activity, and challenges them to apply what they learn to a practical solution. Students will also contribute to community projects that connect their learning to meaningful action beyond the classroom. Through the program, participants will strengthen scientific reasoning, engineering design, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills while developing a deeper understanding of sustainability and how STEM can be used to create positive change. Series Topics: 1. Floodproof! The Science & Engineering of El Niño - November 8; 2. Cooler Cities: Engineering Solutions to Urban Heat - November 20; 3. Clean Air Lab: The Science of Pollution & Filtration - December 13; 4. Microplastics Lab: Investigating Tiny Plastics in Our Environment - December 18. Ages: 7-12. Registration recommended!

events.title: Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion: Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea
events.description: In November, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea by Barbara Demick (2009). The book is based on Demick's interviews over a seven-year period with six North Koreans who escaped the country and the regime. The vast majority of North Koreans know little more of the world beyond their borders than the rest of the world knows about their daily lives under the Kim Jong-il regime. Without easy access to healthcare and with frequent food shortages, life for the average working family in North Korea under Kim Jong-Il's rule is and was grim by Western standards. As of the publication date of this book, ordinary citizens have few if any civil rights and almost no recourse to protest injustice, as complaints and almost any sign of dissatisfaction with the regime could lead to imprisonment. The Adult Nonfiction Book Group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. The group was founded to promote and celebrate the beauty and tradition of Native American social dance and singing styles commonly viewed at Pow Wows. This program is for all ages, and no registration is required! For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: After-School STEaM
events.description: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEaM adventure every week. Active engagement with STEaM promotes academic success. The topic list is subject to change; please check back or call the branch for up-to-date details. Suggested ages vary; please refer to individual program descriptions. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Aug 18 - The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing & Pepper Experiment. Participants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap. Aug 25 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been rescheduled for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly. Sept 1 - Marble Run Fun. Harness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run. Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (please note topic change). In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up. Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time). Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients. Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest. Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch. Sept 22 - Mental Math: Multiplication. Children have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition. Oct 6 - Wind Turbine Engineering. In this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Oct 13 - Paper Rockets. Learn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest! Participants will learn about propulsion, then create their own rockets. Oct 20 - Properties of Water (Science from Scientists). Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion and surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique properties of water. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program. Oct 27 - TBA; Nov 3 - Learn About Aerodynamics Through Paper Planes. In this high-flying workshop, participants will build different types of paper planes and learn concepts of aerodynamics and the impact of plane design through fun and interactive experiments. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Nov 10 - Ozobot Maze Runner. Teach your Ozobot to navigate a maze using simple color codes. Nov 17 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Nov 24 - TBA; Dec 1 - Let's Build Parachutes. In this workshop, participants will build parachutes of different shapes, sizes and materials, and observe the impact of their design. They will participate in fun parachute drops with different loads while learning the science behind parachute design. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Dec 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge. In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.

events.description: Advice | Information | Referral. Social Workers in the Library offers free social service information and referrals*. Our staff can meet with you, approach your needs without judgement, and help you find where to go for shelter, food, showers, mental health services, legal help, and more. Free. No registration required. *Disclaimer: SJPL's Social Work in the Library does not establish a social worker-client relationship. SJPL does not offer case management or extensive follow-up services. We will try our best to get you connected to any resource we know of that could suit your needs. Asesoramiento | Información | Referencia. Este programa ofrece información y referencias de servicios sociales gratuitos. Nuestro personal puede reunirse con usted, abordar sus necesidades sin juicio y ayudarle a encontrar dónde ir para obtener refugio, comida, duchas, servicios de salud mental, ayuda legal y más. Gratis. No se requiere registro. *Aviso: El Trabajo Social en la Biblioteca de SJPL no establece una relación de Trabajador Social-Cliente. SJPL no ofrece gestión de casos ni servicios de seguimiento extensos. Haremos todo lo posible por conectarte con cualquier recurso que conozcamos y que pueda satisfacer tus necesidades. Tư Vấn / Thông Tin / Giới Thiệu Nhân Viên Xã Hội trong Thư Viện cung cấp miễn phí thông tin về những dịch vụ xã hội và giới thiệu. Nhân viên của chúng tôi có thể gặp gỡ bạn, tiếp cận với nhu cầu của bạn mà không đánh giá, và giúp bạn tìm những nơi để đến trú ẩn, thực phẩm, tắm rửa, những dịch vụ sức khoẻ tâm thần, trợ giúp pháp lý, và nhiều hơn nữa. Miễn phí. Không bắt buộc phải đăng ký. Từ chối trách nhiệm: Nhân Viên Xã Hội của SJPL trong Thư Viện không thiết lập mối quan hệ giữa một nhân viên xã hội và khách hàng. SJPL không cung cấp quản lý các trường hợp hoặc dịch vụ theo dõi mở rộng. Chúng tôi sẽ cố gắng hết sức để kết nối bạn với bất kỳ nguồn nào chúng tôi biết có thể phù hợp với nhu cầu của bạn.

events.title: Pow Wow Dance Demonstration
events.description: Please join us for a Pow Wow dance demonstration by Ohiya celebrating Native American Heritage Month! You will learn about the songs, dances, art, food, and traditions of the Indigenous Peoples of America. Ohiya is a cultural collaboration of Native American Singers, Dancers and Artists from the greater San Francisco Bay Area. Guided by our mission: honoring our ancestors and their teachings through cultural expressions of the past, present and future, our group strives to educate people about the songs, dances, art, food, and ways of life of the Indigenous Peoples of America. The group was founded to promote and celebrate the beauty and tradition of Native American social dance and singing styles commonly viewed at Pow Wows. This program is for all ages, and no registration is required! For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Pageturners: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.title: Documentaries: Holodomor Remembrance Day
events.description: The Holodomor, the famine that killed millions of Ukrainians in the 1930s, was not widely known or acknowledged until the fall of the Soviet Union in the 1990s. Established in 1998, Holodomor Remembrance Day is observed on the fourth Saturday of November to remember those who died during the Holodomor. Join us for Palo Alto City Library's second annual program commemorating this event and its lasting effects for some in our community today. Three short documentaries will give us the historical background that reverberates in current events. Descriptions of the documentaries below were written by their creators. Holodomor: How Millions of Ukrainians Died of Starvation During Stalin-Era Mass Famine (Radio Free Europe, 2019, two minutes). Each year, on the fourth Saturday of November, Ukraine remembers the millions who died during the Holodomor, the Stalin-era famine that devastated the population in 1932-1933. Many countries consider it to have been genocide. Minnesota Memories of the Holodomor (PBS, 2025, 26 minutes). In an extraordinary exploration of the transmission of traumatic memory within families, communities and across generations, Ukrainians in Minneapolis-St. Paul share their family stories about the Holodomor artificial famine of 1932-33 and the local community's efforts to come to terms with genocide, even as war once again threatens the existence of Ukrainians as a people. Holodomor: Voices of Survivors (2015, 30 minutes). Twenty-five Ukrainian Canadians tell their stories of survival during the Holodomor--death inflicted by starvation--a genocide of Ukrainian people engineered by Joseph Stalin during 1932 and 1933. Through compelling eyewitness accounts, the film brings into focus a pivotal and little-known period in history, the consequences of which continue to reverberate today. Books on this reading list will be on display and available. Registration is not necessary, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Watch a documentary at Rinconada Library on the Holodomor, the 1930s famine that killed millions of Ukrainians.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to live the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard
events.description: Please join us for an informative workshop presented by UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County. So you want to plant fruit trees? Excellent! What kind? Are you looking for plums, apricots, peaches, apples or something less common? There are hundreds of varieties of each. How do you choose? How big should the tree be? (There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Medicare: Enrollment, 2027 Updates and Plan Review Tips
events.description: The Medicare Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) runs from October 15 through December 7 each year. During this time, Medicare beneficiaries can review and make changes to their Medicare health and prescription drug coverage for the coming year. Join HICAP (Health Insurance Counseling & Advocacy Program) for a free educational presentation covering Medicare updates taking effect in 2027, Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review strategies, and important factors to consider when evaluating your coverage options. Learn how to compare plan costs, provider networks, prescription drug coverage, and other benefits to determine whether your current plan continues to meet your needs. Following the presentation, HICAP counselors will be available for free one-on-one counseling sessions to answer Medicare questions and help attendees review their coverage options. HICAP counselors are unbiased and are not affiliated with any insurance company. The one-on-one sessions will be on a first-come, first-served basis. HICAP is a program of Sourcewise providing free Medicare counseling to Santa Clara County residents. Who Should Attend? Current Medicare beneficiaries reviewing their coverage for 2027; Individuals approaching Medicare eligibility; Family members and caregivers assisting a Medicare beneficiary. What You Will Learn: Medicare updates taking effect in 2027; How the Annual Enrollment Period works; Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review tips; How to compare costs, coverage, and provider networks; Prescription drug coverage considerations; When it may make sense to change plans; Resources and assistance available through HICAP. What to Bring: A complete list of your prescription medications, including dosage and quantity, for accurate plan comparisons. Your Medicare card (optional, but helpful). HICAP counselors will have laptops available for Medicare plan reviews, but attendees are welcome to bring their own laptop or tablet. Time Required: The time needed to complete a plan comparison varies depending on the number of prescriptions and coverage options being reviewed. Most plan reviews take approximately 30–60 minutes. This program is intended for Santa Clara County residents. Please register if you would like to receive a reminder about the presentation. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org. About Sourcewise: Since 1973, Sourcewise has provided services and support to seniors in Santa Clara County. Sourcewise aims to inform, educate, and prepare all adults within Santa Clara County to better navigate their health and life options.

events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Theft
events.description: In November, the Cupertino Library Adult Book Discussion Group will talk about the 2025 novel Theft by Nobel Prize-winning author Abdulrazak Gurnah. Karim and Badar are two young men living on the East African island of Zanzibar. Karim's mother Raya leaves her abusive older husband when Karim is three, taking her son with her. However, when she finds a happy marriage with her new husband Haji Othman, Raya allows her parents to raise her son instead. Years later, when Karim is a university student living with his mother and stepfather for convenience, he meets and befriends the orphaned teenaged boy Badar, whose neglectful relatives force him to become a domestic servant in Haji Othmann's household. There, Badar is treated as a servant, although he is actually Othman's nephew. Fauzia, Karim's beautiful, studious girlfriend, teaches Badar the cooking and housekeeping skills he needs to become a successful domestic servant. Badar's fragile new security is abruptly destroyed when he is accused of theft and dismissed. Even though Karim helps him get a new job at a local hotel, things are never the same between them. Meetings are held in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep them on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Learn how to spot holiday shopping scams and protect yourself online at Rinconada Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Theft
events.description: In November, the Cupertino Library Adult Book Discussion Group will talk about the 2022 novel Theft by Nobel Prize-winning author Abdulrazak Gurnah. Karim and Badar are two young men living on the East African island of Zanzibar. Karim's mother Raya leaves her abusive older husband when Karim is three, taking her son with her. However, when she finds a happy marriage with her new husband Haji Othman, Raya allows her parents to raise her son instead. Years later, when Karim is a university student living with his mother and stepfather for convenience, he meets and befriends the orphaned teenaged boy Badar, whose neglectful relatives force him to become a domestic servant in Haji Othmann's household. There, Badar is treated as a servant, although he is actually Othman's nephew. Fauzia, Karim's beautiful, studious girlfriend, teaches Badar the cooking and housekeeping skills he needs to become a successful domestic servant. Badar's fragile new security is abruptly destroyed when he is accused of theft and dismissed. Even though Karim helps him get a new job at a local hotel, things are never the same between them. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month, on the third Thursday morning at 11 am and on the third Thursday evening at 7 PM. Both meetings are held in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Intermediate Mass Black Holes; Meteor Showers or Space Debris?
events.description: Lecture 1: Understanding how supermassive black holes grow offers key clues to how galaxies evolve, but their "missing link"—intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs)—remains elusive. Because small, blue compact dwarf galaxies cannot host supermassive monsters, they are prime hunting grounds for IMBHs. In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades can reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accreting intermediate-mass black hole at its core. Delivered by Kiera Aston. Lecture 2: Gorgeous meteor showers streaking across the zenith, or space trash entering our atmosphere? The 21st century's growing "space environment" problem is beginning to take center stage. Space debris—artificial spacecraft and objects that have ceased functioning—is accumulating in Low Earth Orbit at an unprecedented rate. We are developing a global space debris monitoring network using ground-based observations. At the core of the system is a three-channel multispectral camera designed to detect the aluminum emission line in the near-UV spectrum, providing a distinctive signature for identifying space debris as it reenters Earth's atmosphere. Delivered by Alice Zou. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear a lecture on how supermassive black holes grow and why intermediate-mass black holes remain so hard to find.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?

events.title: Beyond the Spotlight: One Life. Multiple Passions. Endless Possibilities
events.description: In this inspiring talk with professionals, we explore how passion for the performing arts can coexist with a primary career. Can you be a professional by day and a performer by choice? What does it look like when theater becomes more than a hobby without becoming your full-time profession? Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like. We will discuss how aspiring performers can balance education, professional goals, personal responsibilities, and their love for the stage. Join us for a thought-provoking discussion on pursuing Performing Arts and Theater as a Parallel Career Path: an exploration of passion, purpose, possibility, and the courage to embrace more than one professional identity. Carla Pantoja: Carla, born and raised in the South Bay, is an actor, fight director, teaching artist, intimacy director, and mom of two. She has been a Resident Artist of San Francisco Shakespeare Festival since 2014 and recently served as Director of Vision for the 2021 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Pericles, Prince of Tyre, directing episodes 2 and 4. In 2020, she was in the acting company at Oregon Shakespeare Festival, returning in 2022 as the festival's first female fight director. Carla is an associate instructor for Dueling Arts International and serves on their governing body as President. She is also a proud member of Making Good Trouble, an anti-racist training cohort based in the Bay Area. Carla has directed SF Shakes' Shakespeare on Tour productions of Romeo and Juliet and Comedy of Errors and assistant-directed the 2017 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Hamlet. She played Paulina in Free Shakespeare in the Park's The Winter's Tale, Tybalt in Romeo and Juliet, and Kate in The Taming of the Shrew. She's performed with Cal Shakes, Shotgun Players, Crowded Fire, Playground, Lorraine Hansberry Theatre, and the SF Mime Troupe in the Bay Area, to name a few. Vinay Pande: Vinay Pande is a Silicon Valley technology leader and a passionate theatre artist who brings together the worlds of innovation and performing arts. Originally from Mumbai, India, Vinay holds a degree in Instrumentation Engineering and began his career in telecommunications, where he was part of the core team that developed India's first satellite-based mission-critical voice, data, and video network for the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). He later worked as a researcher at the prestigious Bell Labs, holds 15 technology patents, and has co-authored technical publications and books. Today, he serves as a Principal Architect at a leading technology company in Silicon Valley. Beyond his technology career, Vinay has nurtured a deep passion for the performing arts for over a decade, actively pursuing theatre, acting, and singing across Marathi and Hindi productions. From bringing diverse characters to life on stage to engaging audiences as a Radio Jockey and event host, he thrives on the energy of live performance and the magic of storytelling. For Vinay, technology may be his profession, but the stage is where his creative spirit truly comes alive. Sowmya Renukuntla: Sowmya is a Bay Area native and recent graduate from Santa Clara University, where she studied Business and worked directly with Admission Counselors for four years. Since graduating, she has been working full-time at Levi Strauss & Co. on the Corporate Insights team and is a part-time college counselor. Sponsored by the Cupertino Library Foundation. events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never-before-seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film, including KQED, but national PBS has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers. Registration is not required, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.

Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: Double Play on the Red Line with Raj Oza
events.description: Join us for a special discussion with local author Raj Oza about his book Double Play on the Red Line. Here's a chance to talk to a writer about his writing process and to hear how he came to write this novel. Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Talk with local author Raj Oza about Double Play on the Red Line and hear how he came to write the novel.

events.title: Open Sewing Studio

Use of machines will be on a first-come, first-served basis due to limited supply. Our staff is only available to support very basic projects. Please keep in mind Open Sewing Studio is limited to 1.5 hours.

events.description: Improve your math skills and apply them through fun math-related activities! Participants will focus on a variety of math concepts and do hands-on math activities in this weekly drop-in program. For children in grades 3-5 only. Registration not required. Instruction on the week's concept will occur during the first 15-20 minutes, so please arrive on time. This program meets in person during the school year. We may cancel some meetings due to school/holiday breaks or volunteer unavailability.
events.blurb: Tackle hands-on math activities and concepts each week in this drop-in club for grades 3-5.

events.title: Fiber Arts Circle
events.description: Do you enjoy crocheting or knitting? Want to see what others are working on, refine your skills, or connect with other crafters? Grab your project and join us every week in the Almaden Library living room (behind the Tech Center where the newspapers and magazines are kept) to crochet or knit (or embroider or tat or...) and chat with other crafters making things with yarn. All hand needle crafts welcome. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Almaden Branch Library.
events.blurb: Bring your crochet or knitting project and swap tips with fellow crafters in the library's living room.

events.title: Music and Movement
events.description: Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Free. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Sing songs, trade rhymes, and move along with early literacy activities built for families with kids of mixed ages.

events.title: Stanford Blood Drive

For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.description: Bring your imagination to life with autumn-inspired digital art. We will explore creative tools and techniques using the popular Sketchbook app. iPads are provided for class use. If you'd like to save your project, please feel free to bring your personal iPad or Android tablet (please install the free Sketchbook app prior to the workshop). This introductory class is recommended for ages 7–14 (older siblings welcome). Free. Registration is recommended. Drop-ins are welcome.

events.title: A Look into the Night Sky with Astro Everywhere
events.description: Join us at the Children's Library for a special evening of astronomy with Astro Everywhere! We'll gather in the Treetop Room for a live astronomy show featuring planetarium software to explore the night sky as seen from Palo Alto. Then, head to the Secret Garden for a telescope demonstration and a closer look at the Moon and Saturn. We'll wrap up the evening with a cozy cup of hot cocoa! Thank you to the Friends of the Palo Alto Library (FOPAL) for their generous support.
events.blurb: Watch a live astronomy show in the Treetop Room, using planetarium software to see the night sky as it appears over Palo Alto.

events.title: Tutoring Kidz
events.description: Join us for a fun and exciting tutoring program led by two high school students, Addison and Sarah! Their goal is to make learning an enjoyable and rewarding experience for every student. Through engaging games, creative activities, and interactive lessons, they help students strengthen their English and math skills while building confidence and discovering the joy of learning. Come learn, play, and succeed! Perfect for children ages 5–12! Free. No registration required.

events.description: It's the year of the goat! In this workshop, folks will make a felt goat for Lunar New Year. We will only be hand sewing in this workshop. Open to teens and adults only. Instruments, songs, and dance moves will all be introduced so that everyone will be able to enjoy moving along to the music. This program is meant for families with children, and no previous experience is needed!

events.title: Hip Hop Month: Rap as Storytelling
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Join Veronica Talton, performing arts educator in the Bay Area, as she presents Rap As Storytelling. Her presentation explores the evolution of West African oral traditions which led to the creation of the genre of rap and the widely embraced hip hop culture. events.title: Ukraine: Culture, Geography, History and Heritage
events.description: Nora Mason, a native-born Ukrainian and long-time Saratoga resident, will present a program on the culture of Ukraine and how its geography has contributed to tragic invasions over time. She will share her family's WWII story and how they ultimately immigrated to the United States. She will also touch on inspiring efforts to help the people of Ukraine today. Program co-sponsored by the Los Gatos-Saratoga AAUW.
events.blurb: Hear Ukrainian-born Saratoga resident Nora Mason talk about Ukraine's culture and how its geography has shaped its history of invasions.

In addition to being a great way to introduce the engineering and art concepts of STEAM, playing with LEGOs supports early childhood development because children practice problem solving and teamwork while developing self-confidence and creativity!
events.blurb: Build whatever you imagine from the library's LEGOs on Tuesday afternoons, then snap a photo since creations stay at the library.

events.title: LEGO Club!
events.description: Come join us every Sunday for LEGO Club! We have tons of LEGO bricks for you to build and explore! Duplo bricks are also available for our younger friends. Want to push yourself and try something a little more difficult? Ask the librarian for a LEGO Challenge! Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards.
events.blurb: Build with a huge collection of LEGO and Duplo bricks and try a librarian-issued LEGO Challenge.

events.title: Family Craft: Bean and Lentil Mosaics
events.description: Choose from a variety of beans and lentils to create your own colorful mosaic! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using paper, glue, beans, and lentils. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Design a colorful mosaic from beans and lentils in this hands-on family craft session.

events.title: Print it, Don't Just Think it: 3D Printing and Tinkercad Workshop for Kids
events.description: Come join us for an introduction to 3D printing and CAD! We will learn how to use Tinkercad and how 3D printing works. There will be a live demonstration of the 3D printer working. Free. Ages 8-14. Space is limited; no registration is required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Almaden Library and the SJPL Foundation's Pat Dando Endowment.
events.attendanceNote: Ages 8–14. The library's booking panel requires registration, while its description says no registration is required. Confirm attendance requirements with Almaden Library before going.
events.blurb: Learn Tinkercad basics and watch a live 3D printer demonstration in this beginner workshop.

events.title: Chair Yoga with Patricia Becker
events.description: Join established local yoga teacher Patricia Becker as she takes us through exercises to loosen joints, improve flexibility, improve cognition, and increase strength in Rinconada Library's Embarcadero Room. Registration isn't needed but means you will receive an email reminder. Here are the dates for 2027: January 2; March 6; May 1; July 3; September 4; November 6.
events.attendanceNote: Registration is not required. Optional signup provides an email reminder.
events.blurb: Move through seated stretches with Patricia Becker to loosen joints and build strength in the Embarcadero Room.

events.title: Knitting / Crocheting / Tatting / Bobbin Lace Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts? Join us in the East San Jose Carnegie Branch Community Room every week. Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, or tatting project to work alongside other crafters and swap tips.

events.title: Celebrating Diwali Storytime
events.description: Join us for an illuminating celebration of Diwali during our special storytime at the library. Immerse yourself in captivating tales, vibrant music, and engaging activities that honor the Festival of Lights and the rich cultural traditions of Diwali. Discover the beauty and significance of this joyous occasion as we come together to celebrate unity and light.
events.blurb: Hear Diwali stories and music and join activities honoring the Festival of Lights at this special storytime.

events.title: Village Square Homework Club
events.description: Need room to get homework done and work on class projects? Join us at the Village Square Homework Club. Basic school supplies and snacks are provided. Volunteers are available to help with homework assignments as well. Teens are also welcome to come and work on their school assignments. This program is supported by Friends of Village Square Branch Library.
events.blurb: Get homework and class projects done on Monday afternoons with basic school supplies, snacks, and volunteers on hand to help with assignments.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Friday mornings at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Downtown Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi at Family Storytime on Friday mornings.
