events.title: Game Zone
events.description: Are you an expert at video, board, and card games? Do you want to demonstrate your skills, or just want to learn the basics? Or maybe you'd like to sink the 8 ball at a game of pool? Join us in the Teen Room at the Hillview Branch Library if you want to play video, board, and card games, play some pool, or just hang out! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Play video, board, and card games in the Teen Room, or challenge friends to a game of pool.

events.title: Family Craft: Pom Pom Photo Frames
events.description: Create and decorate a pom pom photo frame! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using popsicle sticks, glue, sequins, buttons, and pom poms. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Decorate a pom pom photo frame with your child using popsicle sticks and sequins at the Children's Library.

events.title: Reading to Children with Kathy
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Sit down with a volunteer reader for one-on-one or small group storytime that builds imagination and a love of books.

events.title: Reading to Children with Aysha
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Read one-on-one or in a small group with volunteer Aysha to build reading confidence and love of books.

events.title: Medicare Mysteries Solved!
events.description: Are you getting ready to apply for Medicare and are confused by the different plans to choose from? Join Sandra Karol, MS, RDMS, RVT, for a monthly workshop and learn more about the different plans that will work best for you and your family. Please register directly with Sandy at isail2@earthlink.net. Attendee limit is 10 people per session.
events.blurb: Learn about Medicare plan options from Sandra Karol in this monthly workshop.

events.title: 1:1 Tech Mentor & Computer Help
events.description: Have a specific tech-related question or just want to learn more about computers and other devices? Come talk to our friendly tech mentor! What We Do: Intro to computer basics; Account or device setup; Intro to Microsoft Office; Job search & resume help; Navigating/organizing email; And more! Free. Register at the 1st Floor Information Desk!
events.blurb: Bring your tech questions to a one-on-one session with the library's tech mentor and get help with computers and other devices.

events.title: Seven Trees Overfelt Adult Education ESL Class
events.description: Free. Placement test and registration required. Learn basic reading, writing, speaking, & listening skills with your library for free! This class meets in person at the Seven Trees Branch Library and is led by a certified English instructor in collaboration with Overfelt Adult Education Center at no cost. Call the library at (408) 808-3056.
events.blurb: Build basic English reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills in a free Overfelt Adult Education class, with a placement test and registration required.

events.title: Wee Love Art: Diwali
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Celebrate the spirit of Diwali with our Wee Love Art program, featuring vibrant Diwali-inspired art activities. Delve into the rich cultural heritage of Diwali as we explore traditional symbols, colors, and motifs through hands-on art projects. Join us for a creative journey that honors the beauty and significance of this festive occasion.
events.blurb: Make Diwali-inspired art projects that use traditional symbols, colors, and motifs, in a hands-on session for young kids.

events.title: Wee Love Art: Diwali
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose

events.blurb: Make Diwali-themed art at West Valley Library in San Jose on Saturday, working with traditional symbols, colors, and motifs in hands-on projects.

events.title: Financial Literacy with Teens Who Invest
events.description: Young adults today in the US are facing social pressures that can compromise their financial well-being. Come learn money matters with Teens Who Invest as they present on how to make good financial choices as teens and adults. Join us every 1st and 3rd Saturday of the month. Recommended for youth ages 10-18 years old. This program is free.
events.blurb: Hear Teens Who Invest present on making smart money choices as teens and adults, with a focus on handling social pressures around finances.

events.description: Celebrate the spirit of Diwali with our Wee Love Art program, featuring vibrant Diwali-inspired art activities. Join us for a creative journey that honors the beauty and significance of this festive occasion.
events.blurb: Make Diwali-inspired art using traditional symbols, colors and motifs in the Wee Love Art program.

events.title: Mandarin Storytime
events.description: Join us for fun stories, rhymes, fingerplays and songs in Mandarin! For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear stories, rhymes, fingerplays, and songs performed in Mandarin at this Saratoga Library storytime.

events.title: Monthly Chat with Mayor Moore
events.description: Get ready to talk about what matters most to you. Mayor Kitty Moore is hosting a Monthly Chat Series in Cupertino throughout 2026, inviting residents and local businesses to discuss any topic with one of the City's decision-makers. These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.
events.blurb: Sit down with Mayor Kitty Moore and raise whatever's on your mind at this informal monthly chat.

events.title: Wee Love Art: Fall Leaf Sensory Painting in Baggies
events.description: Children will put leaf-shaped cardstock into a Ziploc bag and choose fall colors to add in, mixing the paint within the closed Ziploc bag. Kids will experiment with paint mixing, promoting cognitive and social development. Join us for a fun-filled time celebrating fall creativity! Free. No registration required. While supplies last.
events.blurb: Mix fall-colored paint inside a closed Ziploc bag with leaf-shaped cardstock in this sensory art session for kids at Alviso Library.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer. The program will be held under the Read to Children sign within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Join a volunteer for a small-group reading session in Berryessa Library's Children's Area.

events.title: Game On at the Library
events.description: Join us every Sunday at 1:00 p.m. at the Joyce Ellington Branch for a fun afternoon of board games! Choose from our large selection of games, including exciting new favorites and classic games that are fun for all ages. Bring your family and friends, roll the dice, and enjoy some friendly competition! No registration required.
events.blurb: Choose from a large selection of board games and play with family and friends at the library.

events.title: Board Game Zone
events.description: Join us every Sunday between 2:00 and 4:00 PM at the Seven Trees Library to play fun board games! We have a large selection to choose from, including new games and classic games that everyone of all ages can enjoy. No registration required. Thanks to the Friends of the Seven Trees Library for making this possible!
events.blurb: Play board games from a large selection of new and classic titles at Seven Trees Library, with no registration required.

events.title: Journey of finding geodes
events.description: Geodes are as beautiful and diverse as the areas they are found in. Silicon Valley Gem and Mineral Society veteran Steve May will talk about geode formations, how to plan a trip as well as what tools and permits you will need. Join us for a lively discussion. Bring your questions. A Q&A will follow the presentation.
events.blurb: Hear Silicon Valley Gem and Mineral Society veteran Steve May talk geode formation, trip planning, tools and permits, then ask questions.

events.title: Music & Storytelling with Kirk Waller
events.description: Join us for a performance with musician and storyteller Kirk Waller! Kirk mesmerizes audiences of all ages with a dynamic blend of music, movement, and storytelling. Journey with him through captivating tales from long ago and far away, brought vividly to life through his energetic and engaging performance style.
events.blurb: Watch musician and storyteller Kirk Waller mix music, movement, and stories in a performance for audiences of all ages.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Optimizing Social Security Benefits
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a workshop series on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada explain strategies for optimizing your Social Security benefits.

events.title: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month! Story and Craft
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month! We'll be sharing Native American folk tales, then crafting traditional clay pinch pots. Please note that while all ages are welcome, this program is designed for children ages 5 and up. Space and supplies are limited; please arrive on time!
events.blurb: Hear Native American folk tales and craft a clay pinch pot at Palo Alto's Children's Library.

events.title: Tai Chi for Seniors
events.description: Join us at Dr. Roberto Cruz Alum Rock Library for an hour of Tai Chi exercises. Tai Chi improves strength, flexibility, aerobic conditioning, and balance. It's been proven to improve cardiovascular fitness, lower blood pressure, prevent falls, and help people who have arthritis. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Move through an hour of Tai Chi exercises aimed at strength, flexibility, balance, and aerobic conditioning, in a class for seniors.

events.title: Crochet Club
events.description: All are welcome—from beginners to experienced enthusiasts. Bring your own project or start a new one as we refine our skills and discuss all things crochet. A volunteer is available to provide instructions and offer advice to beginners. Tools and supplies are provided. The minimum age is six years old.
events.blurb: Crochet at Tully Library with a volunteer on hand to teach beginners, and use the tools and supplies provided.

events.title: Basic English Level 1
events.description: Learn the basics of English in an inclusive and welcoming environment! You will: • Learn basic vocabulary • Understand simple grammar • Read simple texts and write basic sentences. Lớp này sẽ được giảng dạy bởi một giáo viên có khả năng song ngữ Anh-Việt. Free. Registration requested, but not required.
events.blurb: Build basic English vocabulary and grammar and practice reading and writing simple sentences with a bilingual teacher.

events.title: LEGO Club
events.description: Visit the library every Tuesday for an hour of fun building with LEGO Bricks! Explore your creativity and utilize your engineering skills to build towers, spaceships, forts, and more! This event is recommended for children 5 and older. Small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards for younger children.
events.blurb: Build towers, spaceships, and forts out of LEGO Bricks during an hour of open building time.

events.title: Make Your Own Seasonal Soaps
events.description: In this class, local maker Bea Byrne will guide you through designing and mixing your own personalized soaps. Choose the scents and colors you want, mixing and matching to create unique combinations. Each participant will leave with 3 individual soaps and the know-how to make their own at home!
events.blurb: Mix your own seasonal soaps with local maker Bea Byrne, choosing the scents and colors for your combinations.

events.title: Furry Friends Reading Buddies
events.description: Learning to read is hard, and practicing reading out loud can be a challenge. Kids can come practice reading out loud to dogs. Reading to dogs can help reduce the stress of practicing reading. Children are encouraged to come to the library early to pick their book before the program begins.
events.blurb: Practice reading out loud to friendly therapy dogs in a low-pressure, encouraging setting.

events.title: Learn English: Holiday Fun!
events.description: Are you an adult learning English? Join us for a casual gathering with fellow English learners where you can play games, make holiday cards, learn about American winter traditions, and enjoy holiday music! Registration is optional. If you register, you will receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Practice English with other adult learners while playing games and making holiday cards at this casual gathering.

events.title: Board Game Sunday!
events.description: Everyone is invited to play board games! Join us on the second Sunday of the month from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM. We have board games for all ages: adults, teens, and children. Come with friends & family! (The room closes at 3:30 PM, so come early enough to have time to finish your game.)
events.blurb: Sit down with friends and family to play board games for all ages at the library.

events.title: Chinese Orchestra
events.description: This is an open rehearsal featuring the Chinese erhu (the erhu is a traditional two-stringed bowed musical instrument often referred to as the "Chinese violin"). The public is invited to observe the preparation process for an upcoming performance and participate in a Q&A session.
events.blurb: Watch an open rehearsal of the Chinese Orchestra featuring erhu players and ask questions during the Q&A.

events.title: Chess for Beginners
events.description: Join us for beginner & intermediate chess! Whether you're brand new to the game or looking to sharpen your skills, you're invited to learn and play chess in a relaxed, supportive environment. Walk-ins are welcome, and all materials are provided. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn chess moves and strategy or sharpen your game against other beginners and intermediate players.

events.title: The Peaceful Poets
events.description: The Peaceful Poets are a Milpitas-based group of writers and appreciators of poetry. They welcome all who are interested. The meetings are free. The group meets the last Thursday of every month (except November and December) at 5:30 PM in the Milpitas Library Conference Room.
events.blurb: Share and discuss poetry with fellow writers at the Peaceful Poets' meeting in the Milpitas Library conference room.

events.title: Chair Yoga with Patricia Becker
events.description: Join established local yoga teacher Patricia Becker as she takes us through exercises to loosen joints, improve flexibility, improve cognition, and increase strength in Rinconada Library's Embarcadero Room. Registration is not required, but you will receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Move through seated stretches with Patricia Becker to loosen joints and build strength in the Embarcadero Room.

events.description: Are you between the ages of 5 and 12 and want to learn Vietnamese? Tully Branch Library will be offering a class for children to learn basic Vietnamese language, grammar, spelling, dictation, writing, and reading. In-person registration required at Tully Library.

events.description: Join us on the second Tuesday of every month for an exciting, hands-on exploration of science and technology. From tech-based crafting to interactive robotics, our sessions are designed to keep your mind active and inspired. We look forward to seeing you there!

events.title: Volunteer in the Historic Orchard with UC Master Gardeners!
events.description: The Historic Orchard is a 3.3-acre site planted in 1994 and located in Guadalupe Gardens just south of Taylor Street, adjacent to the Heritage Rose Garden and River Park trails. In the 1930s and '40s, almost everyone who lived here was engaged in the business of fruit production: growing, picking, packing, canning, selling, or otherwise supporting the industry. Today, with very few orchards remaining, this is a place where adults and children can come to experience a piece of local history. Fruit harvested from the Historic Orchard is donated to Second Harvest of Silicon Valley and local shelters. Help us maintain the River Park's Historic Orchard with activities including tree planting and pruning; disease diagnosis and treatment; sun scald prevention painting; sheet mulching; experimenting with different types of irrigation or ground cover; and grafting for improved pollination. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. Restrooms are available at the Rotary Play Garden and will require staff assistance. Address for parking: 438 Coleman Ave. Jose, CA 95110; Meeting location: Historic Orchard (refer to the registration form for a map); Time: 9:30 AM - 11:30 AM; Recurring dates: Every Wednesday
events.attendanceNote: Advance registration is required through Guadalupe River Park Conservancy. Meet at Historic Orchard; see the organizer's registration form for the meeting map. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger.
events.blurb: Join UC Master Gardeners on Wednesday mornings for volunteer work in the Historic Orchard, a 3.3-acre site in Guadalupe Gardens.

events.description: Join us for an afternoon of gardening and grow your skills with guidance from our UC Master Gardener–certified horticulturist! You'll have the chance to learn and practice a wide range of seasonal tasks, including planting, weeding, deadheading, mulching, irrigation, pruning, and more—all while giving a little love back to the beautiful Guadalupe Gardens. We suggest bringing a full water bottle and thick work gloves. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!); Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard); Crafts (in Adobe Room); All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by international Kathak artist Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Celebrate Diwali with the community at Mitchell Park Community Center's Festival of Lights.

events.title: Volunteer in the Historic Orchard with UC Master Gardeners!
events.description: The Historic Orchard is a 3.3-acre site planted in 1994 and located in Guadalupe Gardens just south of Taylor Street, adjacent to the Heritage Rose Garden and River Park trails. In the 1930s and '40s, almost everyone who lived here was engaged in the business of fruit production: growing, picking, packing, canning, selling, or otherwise supporting the industry. Today, with very few orchards remaining, this is a place where adults and children can come to experience a piece of local history. Fruit harvested from the Historic Orchard is donated to Second Harvest of Silicon Valley and local shelters. Help us maintain the River Park's Historic Orchard with activities including tree planting and pruning; disease diagnosis and treatment; sun scald prevention painting; sheet mulching; experimenting with different types of irrigation or ground cover; and grafting for improved pollination. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. Restrooms are available at the Rotary Play Garden and will require staff assistance. events.title: Cielo Hotel Valencia Rooftop Holiday Experience
events.description: November 27, 2026. Beginning November 27, join us Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00–9:00 pm for winter evenings at Cielo Rooftop at Hotel Valencia. The experience will be closed Sundays and Mondays. This holiday season, Cielo Rooftop transforms into an intimate winter retreat high above Santana Row, where seasonal warmth and elevated style come together against the backdrop of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Settle in beneath the open sky and enjoy seasonal cocktails and a curated menu of winter-inspired bites in a warm and inviting rooftop setting. Thoughtful seasonal touches and the glow of the city below create the perfect atmosphere for festive gatherings, date nights, or simply savoring the season.
events.blurb: Spend a winter evening on the Cielo Rooftop at Hotel Valencia, open Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00 to 9:00 pm.

events.title: Line Dancing with Sandy and Kent
events.description: Join Sandy and Kent for a family-friendly line dancing class! Exercise your brain and body and enhance your balance while dancing to a variety of international music. No partner needed and beginners welcome! You are welcome to practice before and after by checking out their special playlist for this class. This class will take place in the Mitchell Park Bowl. (In the event of rain, the class will move to the Midtown Room inside the Mitchell Park Library.) Sandy and Kent have taught line dancing throughout the Bay Area for ten years. Learn more about them on their YouTube channel. Registration is not required. If you register, you will get an email reminder for the program including a link to the class playlist to practice.
events.blurb: Learn line dancing steps with Sandy and Kent to international music; no partner or experience needed.

events.title: Location Change: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Children under 10 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Join Phuong Pham for a mindfulness meditation session at the Art Center Meeting Room.

The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. Please wear appropriate walking shoes and a warm jacket and bring a flashlight or head-lamp. events.title: Noon Year's Eve Celebration!
events.description: Not planning to stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve with your little ones? Then join us for a "Noon" Year's Eve celebration! We will count down to noon on Thursday, December 31, complete with a "ball and bubble" drop. We'll ring in the new year with crafts, dancing and music, so bring your party hats and noisemakers! Come dressed in party attire if you'd like! *This event will be held in the Adobe Room of the Mitchell Park Community Center.
events.blurb: Count down to noon with your little ones, with a ball and bubble drop, so no one has to stay up until midnight.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird ID and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shouldered Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk the riparian trails with Park Rangers on Saturday morning, learning to identify local birds and watching for hawks and owls.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
events.blurb: Watch the true story of Carole King's rise from teenage songwriter to chart-topping icon unfold in song at Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.

events.title: Jane! An intimate exploration of Gilded Age excess and the enigmatic life and death of Jane Stanford
events.attendanceNote: Museum hours: Mon & Fri: 11 AM–6 PM; Thurs: 11 AM–8 PM; Sat & Sun: 10 AM–5 PM. Closed: Tues and Wed.
events.description: Curated by Associate Curator of European Art Patrick R. Crowley, Jane! celebrates the aesthetic and affective excesses of Jane Stanford, the Gilded Age founder and matriarch of Stanford University.
events.blurb: Tour the Cantor Arts Center exhibit on Jane Stanford's Gilded Age excess and mysterious death.

events.title: Electric Contrasts: the Art of the Detail
events.description: Electric Contrasts: The Art of the Detail brings together photobooks and magazines to show how the revolution of photography in the late 19th and early 20th centuries changed the history of art.
events.attendanceNote: Visitors are asked to call 650-723-3408 for building and elevator access to Bowes Art & Architecture Library.
events.blurb: Browse photobooks and magazines tracing how early photography reshaped art history at the McMurtry Building.

events.title: Korean Indigenous Futures: The Art of Kim Bong-Jun
events.description: The East Asia Library at Stanford University will host a print exhibition by Kim Bong-Jun, a leading figure in Korean Minjung (People's) Art, from September 29 to December 11, 2026.
events.blurb: View prints by Kim Bong-Jun, a leading figure in Korean Minjung People's Art, at Lathrop Library.

events.title: Patty Chang: surfacing
events.description: In surfacing, Patty Chang engages the ocean as a physical, geopolitical, and symbolic space, inviting you to consider the work of collection and recollection.
events.blurb: See Patty Chang's surfacing, an exhibit treating the ocean as a physical, geopolitical and symbolic space tied to collection and recollection.

events.title: Green Library Book Display: Witches and Witchcraft
events.description: Green Library's latest book display features books on "Witches and Witchcraft."
events.blurb: Browse Green Library's book display on witches and witchcraft at Hohbach Hall, open as an ongoing exhibit.

events.title: Text Machines: Scarlet Thread of the Digital Order (1883-2026)
events.blurb: Browse the Text Machines exhibit on digital order at Green Library's Bing Wing.

events.title: A Vision of Paris: The Roxane Debuisson Collection at Stanford
events.attendanceNote: Bring a valid government ID and register at the entrance to Green Library to view the exhibition.
events.blurb: View the Roxane Debuisson Collection's vision of Paris at Green Library's Bing Wing.

events.title: In Focus: Asian American Art from the Collection

events.blurb: Browse used adult and youth books, DVDs, and CDs at the Friends sale, with proceeds supporting Mountain View Library programs.
